exposure: Birth setting: Midwifery-based birth center care vs. hospital-based usual care
outcome: Neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission rate
cohort: Women aged 16-45 with low-risk pregnancies (singleton fetus and no record of hypertension or cesarean section) from the American Association of Birth Centers Perinatal Data Registry and birth certificate files (2009-2019), matched using nearest neighbor matching and propensity score weighting
finding: Women receiving midwifery-based birth center care had lower rates of cesarean section, low birth weight, NICU admission, and neonatal death, as well as higher rates of breastfeeding compared to those receiving hospital-based usual care.
mod_finding: Cesarean section rates were significantly lower in the midwifery-based birth center group (-12.2 percentage points, p < 0.001).
